name: t0/greedy
why:
Measured on the 6 probes that spiral, 2 passes each, budget 8000 (hardtemp_q38.json): t0/greedy 10/12 for 35811 tok; t0.6/k20 10/12 for 38126; t0.8/k20 8/12 for 44489; t1.0/k64 7/12 for 52707. Greedy wins on BOTH reliability and cost, and the degradation is monotonic in temperature -- every step hotter answers the same or fewer probes and burns more tokens doing it. This directly contradicts the vendor recommendation: the model card specifies temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20 for thinking mode, and the nearest settings measured here (t0.8/k20 at 8/12, t1.0/k64 at 7/12) are the two worst of the four. That is the second time a Qwen vendor recommendation has lost to measurement on this suite -- on Qwen3.5-9B their suggested t0.6/k20 answered 4/12 where t1.0/k64 answered 10/12, in the opposite direction. The lesson is not 'vendor defaults run hot' or 'run cold', it is that the recommendation is not evidence about this workload either way.

Note on what the 2 unanswered probes are: ts-001 failed 2/2 at EVERY setting, including both temperatures that answered 10/12. It is not a temperature-escapable spiral -- no sampling change reaches it -- so 10/12 is the ceiling here rather than a sign that a hotter draw would help.

Greedy also matches the off arm exactly, so this model's off/on delta is a genuine single-variable measurement: the only thing that differs between its two arms is whether reasoning was suppressed. Same outcome and same reasoning as its predecessor qwen3.6-27b, reached independently by its own sweep rather than inherited.
